query_ground_truth.workflow_task: We need to ingest a large batch of newly updated customer records into Salesforce using the Bulk API, ensuring the job is properly finalized and queued for processing once the upload is completed. Afterward, we need to organize our support communications by creating a dedicated Gmail label for these high-priority customer onboarding accounts so our team can easily track and manage their incoming threads.
query_ground_truth.query: How do I create a new unique label in a Gmail account so I can apply it to incoming support messages?
query_ground_truth.rationale: Creating a new label is the primary step required before managing message categorization in Gmail.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if avoiding duplicates or name conflicts)] [Prerequisite]: Action using GMAIL_LIST_LABELS (scan existing labels by display name and reuse the matching labels[].id instead of creating a new one).
[Required] [Step]: Action using GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL (create the label; immediately store the returned data.id for all later operations; set visibility/color only if needed).

[Optional (for verification or to standardize settings)] [Next Step]: Action using GMAIL_GET_LABEL (confirm properties by id) then Action using GMAIL_UPDATE_LABEL (align visibility/color/settings if mismatched).

[Optional (if labeling existing mail at scale)] [Next Step]: Action using GMAIL_BATCH_MODIFY_MESSAGES (apply the stored label id via addLabelIds across messageIds; batch to tool limits; for conversation-level labeling, use GMAIL_MODIFY_THREAD_LABELS with the same label id).
[Optional (if rollback is required and explicitly confirmed)] [Fallback]: Action using GMAIL_DELETE_LABEL (delete the newly created label by id; destructive).
known_pitfalls: [GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL] HTTP 400/FAILED_PRECONDITION can occur for invalid/reserved names or system-like names; retry with a compliant name.
[GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL] Color/background settings may be rejected if not in the supported palette; if setting colors, provide both background and text values together.
[GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL] 403 permission/delegation errors can occur if the authenticated mailbox context is not the intended one.
[GMAIL_BATCH_MODIFY_MESSAGES] Request keys are strict camelCase (messageIds/addLabelIds/removeLabelIds); using snake_case can fail validation.
[GMAIL_BATCH_MODIFY_MESSAGES] Max 1000 messageIds per call; addLabelIds must be label IDs or the call may 400.

GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL.description: Creates a new label with a unique name in the specified user's Gmail account. Returns a labelId (e.g., 'Label_123') required for downstream tools like GMAIL_ADD_LABEL_TO_EMAIL, GMAIL_BATCH_MODIFY_MESSAGES, and GMAIL_MODIFY_THREAD_LABELS — those tools do not accept display names.

user_id.description: The email address of the user in whose account the label will be created.

label_name.description: REQUIRED. The name for the new label. Must be unique within the account, non-blank, maximum length 225 characters, cannot contain commas (','), not only whitespace, and must not be a reserved system label. Reserved English system labels include: Inbox, Starred, Important, Sent, Draft, Drafts, Spam, Trash, etc. Forward slashes ('/') are allowed and used to create hierarchical nested labels (e.g., 'Work/Projects', 'Personal/Finance'). When creating nested labels, any missing parent labels will be automatically created (similar to 'mkdir -p'). Periods ('.') are allowed and commonly used for numbering schemes (e.g., '1. Action Items', '2. Projects'). Note: 'name' is also accepted as an alias for this field. If a label with this name already exists, returns a 409 conflict; use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to check existing labels and reuse the existing labelId, or use GMAIL_PATCH_LABEL to update it.

text_color.description: Text color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail palette color name (e.g., 'BLACK', 'ROYAL_BLUE'), or exact hex value (e.g., '#000000', '#4a86e8'). If only text_color is provided without background_color, a complementary background color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with background_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. The auto-selected complementary color behavior does not apply; both colors are required.

background_color.description: Background color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail palette color name (e.g., 'ROYAL_BLUE', 'CARIBBEAN_GREEN'), or exact hex value (e.g., '#4a86e8', '#43d692'). If only background_color is provided without text_color, a complementary text color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with text_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. The auto-selected complementary color behavior does not apply; both colors are required.

label_list_visibility.description: Controls how the label is displayed in the label list in the Gmail sidebar. Valid values: 'labelShow' (always show), 'labelShowIfUnread' (show only if unread messages), 'labelHide' (hide from list).

message_list_visibility.description: Controls how messages with this label are displayed in the message list. Valid values: 'show' or 'hide'. Note: These values are different from label_list_visibility - do NOT use 'labelShow' or 'labelHide' here.

GMAIL_LIST_LABELS.description: Retrieves all system and user-created labels for a Gmail account in a single unpaginated response. Primary use: obtain internal label IDs (e.g., 'Label_123') required by other Gmail tools — display names cannot be used as label identifiers and cause silent failures or errors. System labels (INBOX, UNREAD, SPAM, TRASH, etc.) are case-sensitive and must be used exactly as returned; INBOX, SPAM, and TRASH are read-only and cannot be added/removed via label modification tools. The Gmail search 'label:' operator accepts display names, but label_ids parameters in tools like GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS require internal IDs from this tool — mixing conventions yields zero results silently. Do not hardcode label IDs across sessions; refresh via this tool on conflict errors.

user_id.description: Identifies the Gmail account (owner's email or 'me' for authenticated user) for which labels will be listed.

include_details.description: If true, fetches detailed info for each label including message/thread counts (messagesTotal, messagesUnread, threadsTotal, threadsUnread). This requires additional API calls and may be slower for accounts with many labels. If false (default), returns basic label info (id, name, type) which is faster. Counts are eventually consistent and may lag real-time mailbox state by a few seconds.

GMAIL_GET_LABEL.description: Gets details for a specified Gmail label. Use this to retrieve label information including name, type, visibility settings, message/thread counts, and color.

id.description: The ID of the label to retrieve. Can be a system label (e.g., INBOX, SENT, DRAFT, UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM, TRASH) or a user-created label ID (e.g., Label_1, Label_42).

user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.
